title: Rethinking Semi-supervised Segmentation Beyond Accuracy: Reliability and Robustness
mechanism: Reliable Segmentation Score: a harmonic mean of accuracy, calibration and uncertainty quality. SSL methods such as UniMatch V2 gain accuracy and robustness but lose calibration and uncertainty quality relative to supervised training.
adaptation: In the benchmark, report ECE and an uncertainty metric next to crack relF1@2 and inactive IoU for every SSL or FM arm. Calibrated probabilities matter for severity outputs such as inactive area fraction and power-loss band.
min_experiment: No training. Compute ECE and RSS on existing house, PF and ensemble predictions on val/F51, and add them to the benchmark protocol.
evidence: R (from the arXiv page via web search): UniMatch V2 has better predictive performance and robustness but is often less calibrated, with less reliable uncertainty, than its supervised counterpart.

alt_notes.adaptation: Benchmark: report calibration (ECE) and uncertainty quality next to crack relF1@2 for every SSL, ensemble and VFM arm. Calibration also decides how well the val-chosen crack logit bias transfers to E1.
alt_notes.min_experiment: No training. Add ECE and AURC on clean-49 and E1 to the benchmark harness and compute them for the existing house, PF and ensemble predictions.
